c.tagline: Riverside capital of lush Casamance, gateway to Diola villages and the beaches of Cap Skirring.

taxi.fareNote: There are no ride-hail apps in Ziguinchor — agree the fare before setting off. Shared taxis and cars rapides (painted minibuses) run fixed routes for a few hundred francs; hiring a taxi for yourself costs more.

emergency.note: 17 reaches the police and 18 the sapeurs-pompiers (fire and rescue); 1515 is the SAMU medical line. Mobile coverage of these lines can be patchy outside the city.

avoid.reason: Casamance region — occasional separatist activity and rural landmines; check advisories

hood_desc: The compact commercial heart on the Casamance River, around the market, the pier where pirogues land and the gare fluviale; the walkable base where most hotels, banks and restaurants sit and everything is within 20 minutes on foot.
The old African quarter of low tin-roofed houses and lively street life, the traditional cultural core of the town with local eateries and a strong Diola and Mandinka character.
A residential district of shaded compounds and family homes just back from the centre, quieter and local, with small guesthouses and neighbourhood cafés.
A calmer residential and guesthouse area on the town's edge, popular for cultural immersion and longer stays, with easy pirogue access to the mangroves.
A leafy riverside stretch of faded French-colonial villas and the town's better hotels, with gardens and views over the Casamance River; the quietest, most scenic base.

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water only.

transit.hours: Shared taxis and cars rapides run from around dawn until early evening; after dark, chartered taxis are the main way to get around.
transit.note: Ziguinchor has no formal public transport network; getting around means shared yellow taxis and cars rapides (painted minibuses) on the main roads, plus pirogues from the gare fluviale for river trips.
transit.pay: Pay the driver or conductor in cash (a few hundred CFA francs a hop); there is no transit card. Carry small notes.

bus: Sept-place shared taxis & buses to Dakar (via The Gambia)
Cars rapides / minibuses around town and to Cap Skirring
ferry: Pirogues on the Casamance River and to the mangroves

transit.m: Taxi to the city centre (5-10 min)
Shared taxi / minibus toward the centre

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving ~10% at restaurants and for guides is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Saint Anthony of Padua Cathedral
The red-brick cathedral of Casamance's capital, heart of the region's large Catholic community and famous for its joyous choral masses.
Marché Saint-Maur-des-Fossés
Ziguinchor's sprawling central market overflows with mangoes, palm oil, fabrics and Diola crafts—the liveliest few blocks in all Casamance.
Casamance River Waterfront
Watch pirogues and the Dakar ferry ply the broad river from the port promenade, with mangrove birdlife best at dawn.
Alliance Franco-Sénégalaise
A striking cultural center built in Casamance-inspired earthen architecture, hosting concerts, exhibitions and the heartbeat of the region's arts scene.
Village Artisanal
A relaxed craft market where Diola artisans carve masks, weave baskets and dye batiks—watch the workshops, then bargain gently.
Carabane Island
A languid former colonial trading post at the river mouth, with a Breton-style church, slave-trade relics and empty golden beaches.
Mlomp
Renowned for its unique two-story mud houses and a small museum of Diola tradition, set among gigantic sacred kapok trees.
Place Jean-Paul II
A shaded square in the Escale district of downtown Ziguinchor, a gathering spot ringed by colonial-era buildings and street vendors.
Conseil Régional de Ziguinchor
The seat of the Casamance regional government, a colonial-era building officially classified as a historic monument alongside other government structures downtown.
Boulevard du Général de Gaulle
Ziguinchor's grand colonial-era avenue, running through downtown and shaded by towering kapok and mango trees planted alongside government buildings and cafés.

train.note: Senegal has no passenger rail link to the Casamance.

bus.note: Sept-place shared taxis and buses leave the gare routière for Dakar (~10-12 hrs) via the Trans-Gambia Highway and the Banjul crossings, and south to Cap Skirring and Kolda.

intl.to: Dakar (Senegal) - ~15 hr overnight up the coast, avoiding the road through The Gambia
intl.op: COSAMA — tickets at the port office, no online booking

ferry.note: COSAMA's overnight ferries (MV Aline Sitoe Diatta and MV Aguène / MV Diambogne) sail between Ziguinchor and Dakar in about 15 hours, running up the coast to avoid the long road through The Gambia; book cabins ahead.

half.blurb: Traditional Diola (Jola) villages around the old kingdom of Oussouye, with sacred forests, palm-wine culture and impluvium houses, an easy trip southwest.
half.name: Oussouye & Diola villages

half.blurb: A mangrove village reached by pirogue across the Casamance River, known for its striking case à impluvium communal house.
half.name: Affiniam

full.blurb: Senegal's finest Atlantic beaches and a Club Med resort, about 70 km southwest near the Guinea-Bissau border.
full.name: Cap Skirring

full.blurb: A former colonial trading island at the river mouth with a ruined Breton-style church, old cemetery and quiet beaches.
